summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for shortness of breath and chest discomfort following a missed dialysis session. She had a history of paroxysmal atrial fibrillation, systolic dysfunction, and mitral regurgitation. On admission, she was in normal sinus rhythm but had fluid overload, hyperkalemia, and a supratherapeutic INR. A chest X-ray showed small bilateral pleural effusions and bibasilar atelectasis. She underwent hemodialysis, which resolved her symptoms and normalized her potassium. Her metoprolol dose was reduced due to bradycardia and lightheadedness, and warfarin was held due to elevated INR, with plans to restart at 2mg daily. She was discharged home in stable condition with medication adjustments and follow-up arranged with cardiology.
